newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government is set to raise prices of diesel and other "socially sensitive" petroleum products this week because of the recent increase in Singapore posted prices, the new benchmark for domestic pump prices of diesel oil. (TODAY)

- President Fidel Ramos has created a special task force headed by Environment and Natural Resources Secretary Victor Ramos to ensure the efficient development and management of the country's water resources. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The government agency tasked to pursue the assets of the late President Ferdinand Marcos plans to sell its sequestered shares in the Manila Electric Co (TODAY)
- The country's copper production dropped by 82 percent to 41,333 dry metric tonnes in the first seven months of the year compared with 234,923 in the same period last year. (TODAY)

- The International Monetary Fund said the Philippine government needs to earmark at least $5.3 billion for capital expenditures each year over the next 10 years inorder to ease infrastructure bottlenecks in the country. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Manila has unloaded 840 million pesos worth of shares in the Bank of the Philippines Islands. (BUSINESSWORLD)

-The row between the Philippine National Oil Co and Petrochemical Corp of Asia Pacific over the ownership of the $450-million naptha cracker project is feared to delay the implementation of the project.
